title: Design Video Sharing Platform
description:
# Design Video Sharing Platform

Design a video sharing platform that supports uploading videos, removing videos, watching video clips, liking and disliking videos, and querying engagement counters. Each uploaded video is represented by a digit string. The character at index `i` is the content at minute `i`.

Every uploaded video receives an integer ID. The platform must always assign the smallest currently available ID, starting from `0`. When a video is removed, its ID becomes available for a future upload. If that ID is reused, the new video starts with `0` views, `0` likes, and `0` dislikes.

Implement the `VideoSharingPlatform` class:

* `VideoSharingPlatform()` initializes the platform.
* `int upload(String video)` stores `video` and returns its assigned ID.
* `void remove(int videoId)` removes the video with `videoId` if it exists; otherwise it does nothing.
* `String watch(int videoId, int startMinute, int endMinute)` returns the clip from `startMinute` through `min(endMinute, video.length() - 1)`, inclusive, and increases the view count by `1` only when the video exists. If no video exists for `videoId`, return `"-1"`.
* `void like(int videoId)` increases the like count by `1` only when the video exists.
* `void dislike(int videoId)` increases the dislike count by `1` only when the video exists.
* `int[] getLikesAndDislikes(int videoId)` returns `[likes, dislikes]` for an existing video, or `[-1]` when the video does not exist.
* `int getViews(int videoId)` returns the view count for an existing video, or `-1` when the video does not exist.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example 1:

**Input:**
["VideoSharingPlatform", "upload", "upload", "remove", "remove", "upload", "watch", "watch", "like", "dislike", "getLikesAndDislikes", "getViews"]
[[], ["123"], ["456"], [4], [0], ["789"], [1, 0, 5], [1, 0, 1], [1], [1], [1], [1]]

**Output:**
[null, 0, 1, null, null, 0, "456", "45", null, null, [1, 1], 2]

**Explanation:**
The first upload receives ID `0`, and the second upload receives ID `1`. Removing ID `4` does nothing because it does not exist. Removing ID `0` frees it, so the next upload reuses ID `0` for `"789"`. Watching video `1` twice returns clipped substrings of `"456"` and increases its view count to `2`. One like and one dislike make its engagement counters `[1, 1]`.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= video.length <= 10^5`
* The sum of `video.length` over all calls to `upload` is at most `10^5`.
* `video` consists only of digits.
* `0 <= videoId <= 10^5`
* `0 <= startMinute < endMinute < 10^5`
* `startMinute < video.length` for existing videos watched by the judge.
* The sum of `endMinute - startMinute` over all calls to `watch` is at most `10^5`.
* At most `10^5` calls are made to all methods combined.

solutions.name: HashMap and PriorityQueue Free IDs
solutions.timeComplexity: O(log n) upload/remove, O(L) watch, O(1) other queries
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store every active video in a `HashMap` keyed by its video ID. A min-heap stores IDs released by `remove`. On upload, take the heap minimum when one exists; otherwise assign the next never-used ID. Each video object stores content, views, likes, and dislikes together.

## Key Insight

The only ordered operation is finding the smallest reusable ID. Keeping active state in a map and reusable IDs in a min-heap separates ID allocation from video statistics, and removing a map entry before adding its ID prevents double-removal duplicates.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(log n) for upload when reusing an ID and for remove heap insertion, O(L) for watch substring length L, O(1) for like/dislike/stat queries.
- Space Complexity: O(n + m), where n is the number of active or reusable IDs and m is the total stored video content length.

solutions.name: TreeSet Reusable IDs with Video Records
solutions.timeComplexity: O(log n) upload/remove, O(L) watch, O(1) other queries
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a `TreeSet<Integer>` for all currently reusable IDs and a `HashMap<Integer, Stats>` for active video records. Upload removes `reusableIds.first()` when possible, while remove deletes the active record and inserts the ID into the tree.

## Key Insight

A sorted set directly represents the set of holes in the ID space. It makes the smallest-ID rule explicit and also keeps the implementation robust if future operations need to inspect or delete a particular reusable ID.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(log n) for upload and remove because of the TreeSet, O(L) for watch substring length L, O(1) for direct stat updates and queries.
- Space Complexity: O(n + m), for records, reusable IDs, and video strings.

solutions.name: ArrayList Slot Scan Baseline
solutions.timeComplexity: O(V) upload, O(L) watch, O(1) other queries
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store videos in an `ArrayList` where the list index is the video ID. Removing a video writes `null` into that slot. Upload scans from index 0 to find the first null slot, and appends when no hole exists.

## Key Insight

This baseline is slower, but it mirrors the problem statement exactly: the smallest available ID is literally the first empty array slot. It is useful for checking more optimized free-ID data structures.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(V) worst-case upload over V allocated slots, O(L) watch for substring length L, O(1) for valid ID checks and stat changes.
- Space Complexity: O(V + m), for slot records and video content.

solutions.name: BitSet Free Slot Index
solutions.timeComplexity: O(V / word) upload in the worst case, O(L) watch, O(1) updates
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep video records in an `ArrayList`, but store deleted IDs in a `BitSet`. A set bit means that slot is free. Upload calls `freeSlots.nextSetBit(0)` to find the smallest reusable ID, clears it, and writes a fresh video record.

## Key Insight

The BitSet route keeps the array-slot model while replacing linear object scanning with a compact indexed free-slot table. It also makes stat reset natural because reuse writes a new record into the slot.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(V / word) worst-case to find the next free slot, O(L) for watch, and O(1) for removal and stat operations.
- Space Complexity: O(V + m), including the bitset, slot records, and video strings.

solutions.name: Custom Binary Min Heap for Released IDs
solutions.timeComplexity: O(log n) upload/remove, O(L) watch, O(1) other queries
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a `HashMap` for active videos, but implement the reusable-ID min-heap manually with an integer array, `offerFreeId`, `pollFreeId`, `siftUp`, and `siftDown`. Upload polls the custom heap or consumes `nextId`.

## Key Insight

This is the same allocation invariant as a library priority queue, written out to teach the heap mechanics. The heap stores only IDs that were actually removed from the active map, so duplicate stale IDs are avoided.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(log n) for heap push/pop, O(L) for watch, and O(1) for direct stat operations.
- Space Complexity: O(n + m), for active video records, the reusable-ID heap, and video strings.

tests.description: Canonical sample with removal, ID reuse, clamped watch, likes, dislikes, and views.
Removed videos become invalid and the reused ID starts with fresh stats.
Invalid operations do not mutate valid videos, and invalid watches do not add views.
When several IDs are free, upload must reuse the smallest one first.
Likes, dislikes, and views are isolated per video and reset after removal and reuse.
watch clamps the requested end minute to the last available minute and counts every successful watch.
Reusing high and low holes together must still return IDs in ascending available order.
Removing one video does not affect another active video, and the reused ID has empty counters.
